newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS EXPECTED TO RESUME RISE AFTER FAINT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS EXPECTED TO RESUME RISE AFTER FAINT.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, stripped of most of their early gains on Wednesday, are expected to continue their bull run in the next days, dealers said.
At 1530 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.63 percent against 5.60 percent in early business and 5.64 on Tuesday.
"It was just a faint, nothing more," said Dirk Laenen at Cera Bank.
He said a downward correction could be excluded, on the one condition that the upcoming auctions of 10- and 30-year notes in the United States would not cause any difficulties.
The U.S. Treasury will auction some $12 billion of 10-year notes at 1300 EST/1800 GMT in the second leg of its quarterly refunding operation.
"There will be no correction, absolutely, if the paper is absorbed well," one trader said.
Traders noted that business was quiet overall with few institutionals around.

"Normally the months of January and February are the busiest of the year but now activity has dwindled after the first two weeks of January," one said. "There doesn't seem to be much liquidity around," he said.
Traders dismissed chart-technical signals which indicated an overbought situation.
"When we continue like this for a few days, we'll have a nice platform again on which we can build," one said.
The OLO/yield spread, which narrowed to five basis points in the morning, widened again to six in late afternoon business.
The franc, which had firmed slightly to the mark earlier on, weakened again to slightly over 20.63 francs per mark.
But traders dismissed the move as meaningless and said the impact of a recent bribery scandal implicating a government coalition party had waned. -- Bert Lauwers +32 2 287 6815
